correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the Fourier-normalized identity \(\|Tf\|_4^4=\sum_{s,y}|R_f(s,y)|^2\); in odd characteristic midpoint/difference coordinates give \(a^e+b^e=(s^e+h^e)/2\). Multiplicative root orbits have size \(\gcd(e,q-1)\), and an exact sum-of-pair-differences identity yields the displayed nonnegative deficit. A finite-dimensional Cauchy inequality bounds the amplitude term and constant functions attain equality. The gcd dichotomy and trace-phase statements follow by field algebra. A standalone exact checker reproduced nine finite field/exponent cases, including nonprime fields and direct Fourier comparisons; it is not the proof of arbitrary q. For the nonplanar phase group, a Fourier mode calculation reduces any nonconstant real infinitesimal solution to a forbidden multiplier eigenvalue \(\zeta=\pm1\); Smith decomposition of the integer relation lattice then shows projective phase finiteness.

value.rationale: The L2-to-L4 endpoint is a natural nonlinear Fourier extension invariant for Dembowski–Ostrom graph families. The result detects the exact planar/nonplanar transition at all odd prime powers, quantifies a field-theoretic arithmetic jump, and supplies an exact nonnegative amplitude/phase deficit and all-equality phase equations. The nonplanar branch has explicit nonlinear quadratic-trace extremizers, so optimizer geometry cannot be reduced to additive characters or a known unweighted energy count. This is an infinite structural classification, not a small-field lookup. An additional exact integer-lattice/Fourier argument establishes a discrete-versus-continuous topological transition of phase extremizers; after removal of scalar phase, the nonplanar group is finite while the planar phase group is a real torus.
